title: Marking open interpretations reliably
statement: How to mark open interpretations reliably, crediting every defensible reading without forcing one approved answer, and whether a model should do that marking, is unsettled.
detail: The Grade 9 unit's design brief lists judging defensible interpretations without forcing one approved answer among the decisions to make before building (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, line 2893). A later list of gaps says the unit's preparation gives a framework for reviewing an unsupported claim, a misread quotation and a defensible alternative interpretation, but that the browser walk-through of the built lesson did not establish assessment reliability (line 4501). A summary of later meeting notes records that model checks of interpretations were not a settled decision (line 6017).
against: The brief proposes what marking should reward: "Assessment must reward textual fit, justified inference and responsiveness to counterevidence rather than agreement with a model answer." (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, line 3086). That names the target, not a reliable way to mark it.

evidence.quote: How will we judge defensible interpretations without forcing one approved answer?
Our prep gives us a framework for reviewing those cases; the browser walkthrough did not establish assessment reliability.
Removing the Archivist and using LLM interpretation checks were not settled team decisions.
